name: adv_asr_ctc_bad
title: CTC speech recognition with SpecAugment - eleven planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_asr_ctc_clean, hardening round 2, 2026-09-14
note: Round 1's audio pair was a spectrogram classifier; this is the sequence half. Two `unsupported` rows record round-2 findings: DGRG-19 (`torchaudio` is a key in knowledge/__init__._MODULE_FRAMEWORK but has zero knowledge rows, so `_modelled_packages()` counts it as modelled, MLV702 cannot see two torchaudio.transforms modules in a plain list, and no `unresolved_callee` row names torchaudio) and DGRG-20 (MLV112's `_runs_at_import` follows exactly one hop, so a loader built inside `build_loaders()` that `main()` calls is never judged even though the module has no guard at all).

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random
expected.why: the SpecAugment mask positions, the LSTM dropout and the parameter initialisation all move between runs, so two runs report different word error rates from the same data

expected.defect: the device names cuda:0 outright with no availability check
expected.why: the script cannot start on a CPU-only machine

expected.defect: the training loader is built with shuffle=False and no sampler
expected.why: LibriSpeech is stored in speaker order, so every epoch presents whole speakers in a block and the batch gradients are correlated with speaker identity

expected.defect: num_workers=4 and num_workers=2 with no `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard anywhere in the module - main() is called at module scope on the last line
expected.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2 (finding DGRG-20, re-reported as the MLV112 half of the round-2 sweep): `r_data._import_time_chain` now follows the module-scope call chain transitively instead of one hop, so `print(main())` -> `fit()` -> `build_loaders()` is seen for what it is. Original note: MLV112's `_runs_at_import` only fires when the loader's enclosing function is called DIRECTLY from module scope. Here `build_loaders()` is called by `main()`, which is called at module scope: two hops, so nothing fires. Moving the same DataLoader line into main() makes it fire. See finding DGRG-20.

expected.defect: the dev loader shuffles, so decoded hypotheses no longer line up with the utterances they came from
expected.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2 (finding DGRG2-11): `dev` and `devel` are now in `_EVAL_LOADER_RE`, which is reinforcing-only under iron law 2 - it cannot create a tag, only let a finding that already has evidence be seen. Original note: MLV111's `_EVAL_LOADER_RE` is `^(val|valid|validation|test|eval|holdout)_?(loader|dl|data|batches)?$` and does not contain `dev`, which is the canonical name in LibriSpeech, GLUE and CoNLL; the dataset argument carries no VAL/TEST tag because torchaudio is unmodelled. Renaming dev_loader to val_loader makes MLV111 fire. See finding DGRG-21.

expected.defect: the same missing __main__ guard, seen from a second loader
expected.why: LABEL ADDED in hardening round 2: the dev loader requests workers from the same unguarded module, so MLV112 is true of it too. The fix is one guard, so it is `acceptable` rather than a second planted defect - and the row the program's own comment names (line 70) stays `expected`.

expected.defect: the batch loop never calls optimizer.zero_grad()
expected.why: every update applies the sum of every utterance's gradients so far, which with CTC's already large gradients diverges within an epoch

expected.defect: the gradient clipping runs after optimizer.step()
expected.why: the update has already been applied when the clip happens, so the clipping never protects a single step - it only scales gradients that zero_grad would have discarded, if it were called

expected.defect: running_loss is created at line 81, outside the batch loop, and accumulates the live loss tensor
expected.why: every utterance's autograd graph - a BiLSTM unrolled over the whole spectrogram - is kept alive until the epoch ends
the acoustic model carries dropout=0.2 inside the LSTM and an nn.Dropout(0.2) before the head, so every decoded hypothesis is produced with a fifth of the network switched off

expected.defect: greedy_decode() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built for every frame of every decoded utterance and then discarded

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the module moves

forbidden.why: there is no CrossEntropyLoss here at all; the loss is nn.CTCLoss, which takes log-probabilities by contract - the defect at line 88 is that it is given PLAIN probabilities, which is the opposite direction and is recorded under unsupported
there is no binary cross-entropy in this project
the order inside the batch loop is backward (93) then step (94); the clip at 97 is the MLV209 defect, not an ordering inversion between those two
there is no torch.no_grad() anywhere in this file - that absence is the MLV302 defect
OneCycleLR is a per-batch schedule and scheduler.step() is called once per batch, at line 98, which is the correct cadence
there is no GradScaler and no autocast in this project
there is no split call in this project; train-clean-100 and dev-clean are two separate LibriSpeech downloads
Features.__init__ and Acoustic.__init__ both call super().__init__() on their first line
there is no sklearn transformer in this project

unsupported.defect: the two SpecAugment transforms live in a plain Python list, so neither is registered on Features and .to(DEVICE) never moves them
unsupported.why: MLV702 requires the element callee to resolve under `torch.nn.` or to an in-workspace nn.Module subclass. `torchaudio.transforms.FrequencyMasking` IS an nn.Module, but torchaudio carries no knowledge row - and because it is a key in `_MODULE_FRAMEWORK`, `core/unknown_framework._modelled_packages()` treats it as modelled, so not even an `unresolved_callee` diagnostic names it. See finding DGRG-19.

unsupported.defect: one Features module serves both branches and it carries FrequencyMasking and TimeMasking, so the dev word error rate is measured on deliberately corrupted audio
unsupported.why: MLV114 matches a torchvision/albumentations `Compose`; SpecAugment in an nn.Sequential or a plain list on an audio front-end is the same defect in a shape the rule does not read.

unsupported.defect: nn.CTCLoss documents that its first argument is log-probabilities; this passes plain probabilities, so the loss is computed against numbers it reads as log-probs and the gradient points the wrong way
unsupported.why: MLV403 (NLLLoss without a preceding log_softmax) is the nearest code and is a later-tier rule that is not built; no rule covers CTCLoss's input requirement.
